questions.stem: Which is the highest mountain peak entirely within Indian territory (not on the border)?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in the Garhwal Himalayas, Uttarakhand is the highest peak entirely within India. Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is on the India-Nepal border; K2 is in Pakistan-occupied territory.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Nathu La Pass in Sikkim connects India with which country?
questions.explanation: Nathu La (altitude ~4,310 m) connects the Chumbi Valley of Tibet (China) with the Indian state of Sikkim. It was reopened for bilateral trade in 2006 after 44 years. It is one of the highest motorable passes used for trade.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh connects which two regions?
questions.explanation: Rohtang Pass (3,978 m) in the Pir Panjal Range (HP) connects the Kullu Valley in the south to the Lahaul-Spiti valley in the north. It is the main route on the Manali-Leh Highway. The Atal Tunnel was built below it for all-weather connectivity.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Atal Tunnel (Rohtang Tunnel), inaugurated in 2020, provides all-weather road connectivity between Manali and:
questions.explanation: The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km long, world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft) connects Manali (Kullu side) to Sissu in Lahaul valley. It bypasses Rohtang Pass and keeps the Manali-Leh Highway open in winter.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Khardung La, located near Leh in Ladakh, is famous as:
options: One of the world's highest motorable passes (~5,359 m)
The highest peak in the Ladakh Range
A major India-China trade route on the Silk Road
The pass used for troop deployment during the 1999 Kargil War
questions.explanation: Khardung La (Khardung Pass) at approximately 5,359 m is one of the world's highest motorable passes and lies on the route to the Siachen Glacier. It is on the ancient trade route to Central Asia via the Shyok and Nubra valleys.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Zoji La Pass, which is the only pass through the Great Himalayan Range in Jammu & Kashmir, connects:
options: Srinagar to Leh (Kashmir Valley to Ladakh)
questions.explanation: Zoji La (~3,528 m) connects Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley to Leh in Ladakh. It is the gateway to Ladakh from the west and is on NH-1 (Srinagar-Leh highway). The Zoji La Tunnel project aims to provide all-weather connectivity here.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which pass in Sikkim was reopened in 2006 for bilateral trade between India and China, ending a closure of over 40 years?
questions.explanation: Nathu La Pass in Sikkim was reopened in July 2006 for bilateral trade after being closed following the 1962 India-China War. It was historically part of the ancient Silk Road and is one of the highest border trading posts in the world.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Lipu Lekh Pass in Uttarakhand is strategically and spiritually important because:
options: It is the highest pass in India
It connects India to Nepal's capital Kathmandu
It was the site of a key 1965 war battle
It is the traditional route for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra to Tibet (China)
questions.explanation: Lipu Lekh (~5,334 m) in Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, is the traditional route for pilgrims undertaking the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra to Tibet. India and China have agreed to use this pass for trade and pilgrimage. It is also disputed by Nepal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Karakoram Pass, one of the highest passes in the world (~5,540 m), connects which two territories?
questions.explanation: The Karakoram Pass connects the Ladakh region of India with the Xinjiang Autonomous Region of China. It is on the ancient trade route between India and Central Asia (Silk Road) and is named after the Karakoram mountain range.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Mana Pass in Uttarakhand, near Mana village (India's last village on the Indo-China border), connects India with:
questions.explanation: Mana Pass (~5,610 m) near Badrinath in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, is on the India-China (Tibet) border. Mana village, nearby, was historically known as the last village of India on the Char Dham route and a gateway to Tibet.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Sela Pass in Arunachal Pradesh is of strategic military importance primarily because:
options: It connects India to Myanmar via a highway
It is the only border crossing with Bhutan
It provides the main road connection between the Tawang district and the rest of Arunachal Pradesh
It is the highest peak in Northeast India
questions.explanation: Sela Pass (~4,170 m) in West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh is the primary road link between Tawang (near the McMahon Line) and the rest of Arunachal Pradesh. The Sela Tunnel project aims to provide all-weather connectivity to Tawang.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Shipki La Pass in Himachal Pradesh is used as a trade route between India and:
questions.explanation: Shipki La (~5,669 m) in Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Sutlej River, is a traditional trade route between the Spiti valley of HP and Ngari Prefecture of Tibet (China). The Sutlej (Langchen Khabab) enters India through this pass.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m), the third-highest mountain in the world, is located on the border between:
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga is on the border of Sikkim (India) and Nepal. It has five summits; the main summit (8,586 m) is the highest point in India. The name means 'Five Treasures of Snow' in Tibetan.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Karakoram Range, containing some of the world's highest peaks, is located in which part of India?
questions.explanation: The Karakoram Range lies in the Ladakh region. It contains K2 (8,611 m), the world's second-highest peak, in Pakistan-administered territory. The Siachen Glacier and the Saltoro Ridge, contested by India and Pakistan, are also in this range.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: K2 (Godwin-Austen), the world's second-highest peak (8,611 m), is currently located in:
questions.explanation: K2 is in the Karakoram Range in the Gilgit-Baltistan region, which is administered by Pakistan but claimed by India as part of the state of Jammu & Kashmir. Also known as Godwin-Austen or Chogori, it is the hardest of the eight-thousanders to climb.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Diphu Pass, located at the trijunction of three countries — India, China, and Myanmar — is in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Diphu Pass (also called Dapha Bum area) is at the tri-junction of Arunachal Pradesh (India), Yunnan/Tibet (China), and Kachin State (Myanmar). This sensitive border area has been a matter of strategic interest for India.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Bara Lacha La Pass is located on the Manali-Leh Highway in which state/UT?
questions.explanation: Bara Lacha La (~4,890 m) is located in Lahaul-Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh on the Manali-Leh Highway. It is a watershed pass from which rivers flow in four directions (hence 'bara lacha' = pass with roads going in multiple directions).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Himalayas are traditionally divided into three parallel ranges from north to south. These three main divisions are:
options: Greater Himalayas (Himadri), Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and Outer Himalayas (Shivalik)
Eastern Himalayas, Central Himalayas, and Western Himalayas
Alpine zone, Temperate zone, and Subtropical zone
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are divided into: (1) Greater/Inner Himalayas (Himadri) — highest, permanently snow-covered; (2) Lesser/Middle Himalayas (Himachal) — 1,000–4,500 m, includes major hill stations; (3) Outer Himalayas (Shivalik/Sub-Himalayas) — 900–1,200 m, lowest range.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve (UNESCO World Heritage Site), surrounding India's highest entirely-within-India peak, is located in:
questions.explanation: The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is in the Chamoli and Pithoragarh districts of Uttarakhand. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988 (and extended to include the Valley of Flowers in 2005).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Pir Panjal Range, which contains the Rohtang Pass and Banihal Pass, is part of which Himalayan sub-division?
questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal Range is a sub-range of the Lesser/Middle Himalayas (Himachal Himalayas), lying to the south of the Greater Himalayas in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. The Banihal Pass on this range provides the Srinagar-Jammu highway route.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Aravalli Range, one of the world's oldest fold mountains (~350 million years old), runs through which states?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range runs from Gujarat in the southwest through Rajasthan (its main extent), Haryana, and ends near Delhi (Raisina Hill). Gurugram and south Delhi hills are remnants of the Aravallis. The highest peak is Guru Shikhar (~1,722 m) in Rajasthan.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: In the Himalayan geography, 'Duns' are longitudinal valleys found between which two ranges?
options: Shivalik and Lesser Himalayas — e.g., Dehradun
questions.explanation: Duns (or Doons) are flat-floored, synclinal valleys between the Shivalik range and the Lesser Himalayas. Famous examples: Dehradun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun. Dehradun, where Doon School is located, is the best-known Dun valley.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Western Ghats (Sahyadri Range) run parallel to which coast of India, acting as a barrier to the southwest monsoon?
options: East coast (Coromandel / Bay of Bengal coast)
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run along the western edge of the Deccan Plateau, parallel to the Arabian Sea coast. They extend from the Tapti River in Gujarat/Maharashtra in the north to the Nilgiris-Palakkad Gap area. They force the southwest monsoon to rise and deposit heavy rainfall on the western slopes.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats of India meet at which hills in Tamil Nadu/Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Eastern and Western Ghats converge at the Nilgiri Hills in the junction of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala. Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak of the Nilgiris. Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is located in the Nilgiri Hills.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, located near Ooty (Udhagamandalam) in Tamil Nadu, is:
questions.explanation: Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills and the second-highest peak in the Western Ghats (after Anaimudi). Anaimudi (2,695 m) is the highest peak in the Western Ghats and all of peninsular India, located in the Anaimalai Hills (Kerala), not the Nilgiris.
questions.subject: Geography
